summary.headline: FY26 revenue rose 14% to INR931 crore and EBITDA margin expanded 405 bps to 7.7%, while Q4 volume fell to 1,912 MT from 2,349 MT.
summary.overview: Apex Frozen Foods reported FY26 revenue of INR931 crore (up 14% YoY) and EBITDA of INR73 crore (up 145%), with PAT of INR39 crore versus INR4 crore. Q4 FY26 revenue was INR168 crore versus INR197 crore, on volume of 1,912 MT versus 2,349 MT, while Q4 EBITDA margin rose to 9.8%. Non-US markets, led by the EU (up 19% in FY26, 15% in Q4), became the largest sales contributor at about 52% for the first time, as US volumes fell on tariffs and logistics disruption. Management expects US volumes to recover now that tariffs have fallen to about 10%, and it is targeting roughly 30% volume growth in FY27, though it said this is subject to production and shipping constraints.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR197 crore in Q4 FY25

segments.name: US market
segments.commentary: Volumes fell due to IEEPA tariffs (peaking near 50%, now about 10%) and logistics disruption; management says orders are returning. US revenue was about INR500 crore versus about INR700 crore previously, per an analyst's estimate.

segments.name: European Union
segments.commentary: EU grew 19% YoY in FY26 and 15% in Q4 FY26; management says the EU accounts for about 50% of total volume. UK FTA is expected soon and EU FTA around end of calendar 2026.

segments.name: Ready-to-eat
segments.commentary: RTE was 12% of revenue mix in FY26, up from 10% in FY25.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume expected to rise, with management originally envisaging about 30% volume growth; a planned volume of around 14,000 MT was mentioned, subject to production and logistics.
Management said FY26 EBITDA margins should be sustainable if markets remain stable, but gave no formal FY27 margin guidance.
US volumes expected to recover following tariff reduction to about 10%; a US-specific FTA is not yet defined.
New markets such as Russia are being approved for both facilities.
Export incentive (rebate of indirect taxes) expected at about 5% to 6% of exports, subject to caps and no policy change.
capex_capacity: Both facilities are operating in the summer crop season after a brief consolidation period in FY26.
Capacity utilisation was about 30% for the full year FY26, leaving headroom for growth.
Q4 volume was affected by worker-related issues in January and February; volumes recovered in March.
Shipping equipment shortages and vessel schedule delays are postponing shipments by 3 to 5 days.
demand_pricing: Average realisation was about $9.5/kg in FY26 and about $9.1 to $9.2/kg currently; INR830/kg realisation in Q4 FY26 versus INR348/kg average farm-gate procurement cost.
Full-year FY26 farm-gate price averaged INR327/kg; Q4 averaged INR348/kg; Q1 FY27 is expected around INR340/kg.
Management said depreciating rupee is partly passed on to farmers and competitors, and realisations lag orders by 70 to 90 days.
Forward cover is about 30% to 32% of exposure.
Management said freight costs have risen marginally, with the Middle East crisis affecting shipping lines' equipment availability.

qa_highlights.question: Will US revenue return to about INR700 crore once tariffs ease?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said US volumes will scale back up, and revenue will follow based on dollar unit values and currency realisation; tariffs are now about 10%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the EBITDA margin sustainable and what drove the margin gain?
qa_highlights.answer: Drivers were inventory from earlier quarters, lower debt cost, process efficiencies, favourable raw material pricing and rupee depreciation; management said margins should hold if markets are stable.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 volume fall while gross margin improved?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited January worker issues and holiday-period disruption; margin was supported by stable farm-gate prices and inventory use.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 volume outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects an increase in volume, originally envisaging about 30% growth, with US recovery and EU/UK FTAs as drivers, subject to production and logistics.

qa_highlights.question: What is the export incentive outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Rebate of about 5% to 6% of exports, subject to caps and no policy change; management described it as a duty reimbursement rather than an incentive.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Middle East impact on logistics?
qa_highlights.answer: Freight costs rose only marginally; the main issue is shipping line equipment shortages causing 3 to 5 day shipment delays.

risks_watch: Pace of US volume recovery after tariff reduction and any US trade agreement terms.
Shipping equipment shortages and Middle East-related logistics delays affecting shipment timing.
Rupee movement: only about 30% to 32% of exposure is hedged, and management declined to predict Q1 realisation (analyst estimate of 7% to 10% rupee realisation increase was not confirmed).
Farm-gate price trends and government feed-price measures in Andhra Pradesh.
Non-recurrence of FX gains: other income of about INR17 crore was mainly forex difference gains.
Sustainability of margin, which management linked partly to inventory usage and favourable raw material prices.
summary.management_tone: Confident on diversification and recovery, but cautious on logistics and macro uncertainty. Management was direct on pricing and margin drivers, but avoided commenting on competitors and gave no formal FY27 margin guidance.
key_quotes: For the first time in Apex's history, non-U.S. export markets became the largest contributor to sales in FY '26, accounting for almost 52% of the total sales mix.
So we are optimistic, but at the same time, we are also being cautious.
We are getting back our orders from the U.S. market also.
